Where I got to
I stopped mid-slice at the tool limit. Here's the state, so you can decide whether to have me finish it in the next turn.

Reconstruction and drift
dump.txt reconstructed cleanly: 380 files, SHA-256 verified, only export.sh (self-referential — it contains its own ${SCRIPT_NAME} record) and LICENSE (elided by design) mismatch. Both benign.

My session memory was drifted by two slices — it said Slice 60 / spec v1.45. The tree is at M6 Slice 62, spec v1.47, predicted 1296 tests, §16.3 at 21 scenarios. Carried baseline, not measured.

The failure, diagnosed
src/MyRestaurant.WebApplication/Security/RateLimitedSurfaces.cs:23
    /// The policy name. The page opts in with <c>[EnableRateLimiting(…)]</c> naming this value, the
RateLimitingContractTests.OptIn is EnableRateLimiting\(\s*([^)]*?)\s*\), and its own summary claims the open parenthesis makes it safe on F-67's authority. That claim is false. F-67 is about an identifier — Foo( vs Foo. It does not transfer to a form: a documentation comment explaining an attribute spells the attribute, placeholder argument included. So the gate reported a finding on a correct tree on its first real run, and the argument it reported was a horizontal ellipsis.

This is not your hand-fix. It shipped in Slice 62, in the gate and the file that gate protects, in the same archive. Slice 62's sensitivity emulation claimed to walk "the same files with the same pattern" and did not reproduce it — the emulation was written against the tree the session imagined, not the one it shipped. That is the part worth recording.

Confirmed by scan: 3 raw matches under src/, 2 real opt-ins, 1 prose.

What I built and verified
The remedy is a reader, not a reworded sentence — SourceCode.WithoutComments, a comment-blind source reader that both gates scan through, so there is one decision procedure rather than two that can disagree. Validated by transcribing the C# back to Python line-for-line and running it over all 169 .cs/.razor files under src/: EnableRateLimiting( 3→2 with both arguments correct, newlines preserved in every file, no file emptied, structural tokens intact in the raw-string, CSS-comment, and Razor-comment-block files.

Menu progress: Stage 6b — Stage 6's prerequisite 4 (§11.11's rendering rule) discharged before comments exist, which is the shape Stage 6a used for prerequisite 1. §17 has claimed since Slice 24 that raw HTML is a closed set, written as "the six MarkupString sites" in four places and enforced in none — F-112's shape a fourth time. RawHtmlContractTests holds the set instead; the live copies of the count are deleted.

Seven planted defects, each caught by the intended assertion: a new raw-HTML site on the guest menu, a recorded site deleted, a second production in a recorded file, a bare-literal opt-in, an unregistered member, the reader made a no-op, the reader emptied. D6 matters — with the reader disabled, both prose mentions reappear as findings, so keeping them in the tree makes the remedy load-bearing rather than theoretical.

A third finding on the way in (F-93's timing again): §16.4 says the response-header tests are "three classes in the unit job… three rather than one". Slice 62 made that four. This slice would have made it five. No gate can see it — it is a count of paragraphs about a directory.
